review_title: Allow Customers Recite The Big Mac Jingle
review_details: Allow Customers Recite The Big Mac JingleThe latest Big Mac promotion by McDonald's is nothing short of disappointing and deceptive. Their TV commercial presents an enticing offer: recite the Big Mac ingredients jingle in 4 seconds at a McDonald's restaurant, and receive a complimentary small fries and Coke. As someone who has had the jingle memorized since the 1970s, I was eager to participate after half a century of anticipation.However, my excitement quickly turned to disillusionment upon further investigation. Instead of the expected inte... Read moreraction at the counter, I discovered that the promotion is entirely app-based. Rather than verbally reciting the jingle, customers are presented with a digital puzzle where they must rearrange text boxes representing the jingle in the correct order within a mere 4 seconds. This not only eliminates any human interaction but also feels like a deliberate attempt to mislead customers. McDonald's has essentially stripped away the essence of the promotion, denying customers the opportunity to engage in the nostalgic act of reciting the jingle aloud. It's baffling that in this age of advanced technology, they couldn't incorporate a simple recording feature into their app to allow customers to verbally participate. In essence, this promotion feels like a facade, promising one thing but delivering another entirely. McDonald's owes its customers transparency and authenticity, neither of which are present in this misleading campaign. It's a shame to see such a beloved brand resort to such tactics, tarnishing the fond memories many of us have associated with the Big Mac jingle.
keywords: misleading promotion | app-based puzzle | false advertisement | no human interaction
summary: Big Mac jingle promotion advertised as verbal recitation but actually requires app-based text puzzle.

review_title: Big Mac should be rename Little Meat
review_details: Big Mac should be rename Little MeatLunch at McDonald's Port Augusta as we've done many times on our way through from Adelaide to Port Lincoln. Easy to order, quick service but that's where it ends. Indifferent staff did not respond or acknowledge our "thank you". Prices were high for fast food. Big Mac was small and the two beef paddies we're extremely thin, lucky to be 5mm thick.Ok the coffee is good.Anyway we won't be visiting McDonald's again, Hungry Jack is better value which is a pity after near 50 years of patronage.
categories: Food Quality | Portion Size | Price Value | Service Speed | Staff Behavior
keywords: quick service | small Big Mac | thin beef patties | indifferent staff | high prices | good coffee
summary: Quick service and good coffee offset by small Big Mac, thin patties, indifferent staff, and high prices.
